text:
Dallas spent the first half of November without Miro Heiskanen, and his return was instant theater: an overtime winner against Vegas on Nov. 17, then the opening goal against the same Golden Knights two nights later. Since coming back he's played 26 to 29 minutes a night, which tells you how much the Stars missed him.

The goals deserve a caution. He has 5 on 2.2 expected and is shooting 15% after 6% last season. That rate rarely lasts for a defenseman, and we'd expect his scoring to drift back toward assists. The underlying game is the reason not to worry: Dallas takes 54% of the 5v5 expected goals with him on, nearly six points better than without him.

Evolving-Hockey had him 12th among 215 defensemen last season, with a big chunk from the power play and more penalties drawn than taken. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds one thing to watch: he shoots a lot from the point but not often from the slot. The last two games were both losses, so the Stars will lean on him again.
